subject: Re: Veridian Health — data controls & logging constraints (post-call recap)
messages:
From: Alex Moore <alex.moore@veridianhealth.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@veridianhealth.com>
Date: 2026-11-28T14:05:00-05:00
Subject: Intro + discovery call request — Veridian Health logging constraints

Hannah — thanks for taking time to connect today. We run a mix of legacy services and a new FHIR-based ingestion pipeline; we're evaluating vendors who can serve real-time inference for clinical triage but also meet our strict audit and retention policies.

Primary asks for the call:
- Understand how Redwood handles PII in logs and traces (are logs redacted before persisting?)
- Retention controls and per-customer retention windows
- Audit log granularity (who accessed which request, token-level traces?)
- Encryption / KMS options and ability to bring our own key

I've attached our current logging policy for context (veridian-current-logging-policy.pdf). Can we schedule a 30-minute discovery this week?

—Alex
Alex Moore
Senior Engineering Manager, Data Platforms
Veridian Health
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Moore <alex.moore@veridianhealth.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@veridianhealth.com>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-29T10:12:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Intro + discovery call request — Veridian Health logging constraints

Alex / Priya — great speaking with you earlier. Below is a concise recap of the topics we covered, our understanding of Veridian's constraints, and proposed next steps. Please flag anything I missed or mischaracterized.

Summary of pain points and goals
- Pain: Current pipeline emits structured logs that may include PHI in certain fields; Veridian must avoid persisting any raw PHI in third-party systems and needs defensible audit trails.
- Goal: Real-time inference for clinical triage while guaranteeing no PHI is written to vendor logs/storage and preserving a 90-day retention window for non-sensitive metadata and a 0–7 day window for any traces that could be reconstructed.

What Redwood can offer (high-level)
- Redaction hooks: runtime request/response redaction before logging (customer-controlled rules + allow-listing).
- KV / prefix caching disabled for PHI-labeled routes; per-route cache and batching controls.
- Retention controls: configurable per-customer retention policy in Private and Dedicated deployments; hosted customers get policy controls and guaranteed deletion endpoints.
- Audit logs: token-level audit with role-based access, immutable append-only audit stream exportable to your SIEM.
- Encryption: support for customer-managed keys (KMS) in Private deployment; hosted KMS options and envelope encryption for payloads.

Open items we discussed (items needing confirmation)
1) Required retention windows: you mentioned 90 days for non-PII metadata and 7 days for potentially identifying traces — please confirm exact buckets and regulatory drivers.
2) Redaction patterns: we should validate which fields in your ingestion pipeline are considered PHI so we can propose exact redaction rules.
3) Log export format: you asked for a daily export (S3) and a streaming audit feed (Kafka) — confirm both endpoints.
4) SOC 2 / HIPAA: you indicated Veridian requires evidence for HIPAA controls — we will gather relevant SOC 2 reports and our HIPAA-attestation summary; scope will depend on deployment mode.

Proposed next steps
- Action 1 (Veridian): Send a quick list of 6–8 example log fields that might contain PHI and the desired retention buckets. (Owner: Priya, ETA: 2026-12-03)
- Action 2 (Redwood): Provide a short redaction/retention checklist and two sample configurations: Hosted (with deletion endpoints) and Dedicated (reserved) options. Attach: redaction-requirements-cheatsheet.pdf (Owner: Hannah, ETA: 2026-12-02)
- Action 3 (Joint): Tech deep-dive with our Solutions Engineer (Marcus) to validate integration points and sampling strategy. Suggest 45-minute session the week of 12/7. (Owner: Marcus / Veridian)

Hannah / Sergio — forwarding the recap so I can prepare for the joint deep-dive. Notes for the session prep:
- Ask Veridian for a small redacted sample of their logs (already requested by Hannah). If they can't share full samples, a schema + example rows is fine.
- Prepare a short demo showing: 1) request-time redaction rule being applied; 2) audit log entry generation; 3) how retention rules remove entries from the hosted store.
- Raise questions on whether they need guaranteed zero-copy on disk for PHI (this is typically Private deployment territory).

Attachments: redaction-requirements-cheatsheet.pdf (internal version)

—Marcus

Subject: Re: Veridian Health — data controls & logging constraints (post-call recap)

Hannah — thanks for the detailed recap and quick turnaround. Confirming next steps from our side:
- We'll deliver 6 example fields plus a redacted daily log sample by 2026-12-03.
- Procurement copied here; they will request a short T&Cs overview + any HIPAA applicability notes for initial review.
- We prefer to see a demo on 2026-12-09 or 12-10 (45 minutes). Marcus — can you do 12/09 11:00am ET?

One clarification on retention: our security policy requires a formal justification for any retention beyond 7 days if logs contain reconstructable PHI. If Redwood can demonstrate redaction at ingest with attestable deletion flows, that may allow the 90-day metadata bucket you described.

Attachment: veridian-sample-logs-scrubbed.zip (redacted sample)

Thanks,
Priya Shah

Veridian Health
